newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SBC H1 CHEERED AS BEST SWISS BANK RESULT.
newsitem.headline: SBC H1 CHEERED AS BEST SWISS BANK RESULT.

text.p: Analysts cheered the first half results of Swiss Bank Corp (SBC), the smallest of Switzerland's Big Three global banks, as the best of the lot.
SBC net profit surged 84 percent in the first six months against a year earlier, compared with a 70 percent jump at Credit Suisse Group and 67 percent at Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS ).
"It is clearly the best result of the three big banks," Zurich Kantonalbank analysts Christoph Bieri told Reuters.
"There is nothing in the details that would bother me. This result was genuinely achieved at the operating level," he said.
Hans Kaufmann from Bank Julius Baer in Zurich said he would have to raise his full-year net profit forecasts by 10 to 20 percent.
"I'm very happy about this result," Kaufmann told Reuters.
"I was in the upper third of the consensus forecasts, so the majority of analysts will probably have to raise their earnings estimates substantially," he said.
Kaufmann has so far put 1997 net profit at 1.877 billion Swiss francs or 23.9 francs per SBC share.
"Also, gross profit was significantly stronger than the two other banks," Kaufmann said.
SBC said gross operating profit was up 27 percent to 2.617 billion francs. At UBS, operating profit was up only 8.5 per cent while CS Group reported a gain of 23 percent.
"Trading and commission income were substantially better than expected. Interest income was more or less in line," Kaufmann said.

Costs, especially personnel costs driven by performance bonuses for traders, were substantially above estimates. Total operating expenses rose 29 percent to 4.2 billion Swiss francs including a 31 percent jump in personnel costs.
"But the cost problem seems to be a problem for all banks. My guess is that every bank makes provisions for bonus payments," he said.
Kaufmann had forecast half-year net profit growth at 51 percent, at the lower end of a range from 50 to 70 percent. Zurich Kantonalbank's Bieri was at the top with a forecast of 70 percent.
Both Kaufmann and Bieri said SBC would remain a "buy" recommendation.

Bieri switched the two other big banks around after both reported half-year results in the past two weeks and after CS Group said on Monday it was buying major Swiss insurer Winterthur in a stock-only deal.
"I moved CS Group down to hold and raised UBS to buy," Bieri said.
